clue.text: A Sikh on vacation engaged by, for instance, leisurely walk

indicators.note: something engaged by another is held within it, as a cog is gripped, so the first part sits inside the second

parts.note: 'say' introduces an example, just as 'for instance' does

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Sikh man out on holiday takes an unhurried stroll, perhaps along a promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' means emptied, keeping only the outside letters of Sikh; 'engaged by' sets those, after A, into the word for 'for instance'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a casual, swaggering or unhurried manner; here used as a noun for such a stroll.

clue.text: Fail to keep appointment with last of mandarins in Whitehall etc

parts.note: to stand someone up is to miss a date with them

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Senior civil servants in Whitehall, the British government district, miss meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall looks like the government district; it is Jack Whitehall, a British stand-up comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Whitehall is an example of stand-up comedians, so 'Whitehall etc' are stand-ups.

clue.text: Essential matter overlooked by group as key moment in a court?

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece overlooked by another sits beneath it

parts.note: a set is a group
the point is the essential matter in a discussion

explanation.surface: A key point in a legal case is missed by a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, a set point is the moment a player can win the set.

clue.text: See eye to eye with a native of Corfu largely

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: Corfu is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Getting along with a local on Corfu, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: To see eye to eye is an idiom for being in agreement.

clue.text: A belief in reform around Sweden is likely

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the Swedish abbreviation, enclosing it
a belief in reform is being reshaped, so its letters along with A are rearranged

parts.note: S is the international vehicle registration letter for Sweden

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a belief in reforming Sweden is plausible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In reform' rearranges A BELIEF to FEAIBLE; 'around' puts that round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something feasible is possible and practicable, close in sense to plausible or probable.

clue.text: A tune played with levity as a possible result

indicators.note: a tune played freely is reworked, so its letters are rearranged with the others

explanation.surface: A tune played light-heartedly might be one outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventuality is something that may happen, a possible outcome.

clue.text: Wild prank in sea, not a feature of yachting?

indicators.note: wild letters run free, rearranged out of their order
not means a letter is subtracted from the anagram pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: A wild joke at sea is not part of sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges PRANK IN SEA once 'not' has taken out one A.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinnaker is a large balloon-shaped sail used on yachts when running before the wind.

clue.text: British comedienne dropping very old sitcom actor

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Joan Rivers was a famous comedienne

explanation.surface: A British comedienne leaves out a veteran sitcom star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' takes V from RIVERS. Richard Briers starred in the British sitcom The Good Life.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Briers, who died in 2013, was a well-loved actor in sitcoms of earlier decades.

clue.text: Former partner leads number wanting hotel in English city

indicators.note: one piece leads, coming before the other

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: ether is a number, an anaesthetic that numbs
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An ex-partner leads a figure looking for a hotel in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a figure; it is something that numbs, ETHER. 'Wanting' removes H, leaving ETER.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, England.

clue.text: A second seabird on the back of a liner, say

definitions.text: on the back of a liner, say

parts.note: a tern is a common seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird perches briefly at the stern of an ocean liner.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for at or towards the rear of a ship, of which a liner is one example.

clue.text: What initiates disquiet about fellow in computing etc for certain

indicators.note: one piece goes about, that is around, the rest of the letters

parts.note: the word disquiet begins with D, whose letter name is spelt DEE
IT, information technology, covers computing and the like

explanation.surface: Something causing unease about a man working in computing is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter that begins 'disquiet' is spelt out as its name rather than written as one letter; 'about' then wraps that name around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Definite means certain or settled; something known for certain is definite.

clue.text: Bodies not disposed to make a useful contribution

indicators.note: letters disposed are arranged afresh, laid out in a different order

explanation.surface: Some people simply aren't inclined to pull their weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not disposed' reads as reluctant, but 'disposed' is the anagram signal for BODIES NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To do one's bit is an idiom for playing one's part or helping a shared effort.

clue.text: Traditional site for an engagement?

parts.note: an engagement suggests a betrothal, but here it is a military engagement, a battle, fought on open ground

explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is also a military clash, and such clashes take place on open ground.

clue.text: Bottle stocked by finer vendors

indicators.note: an item stocked by a shop is held inside it, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: A bottle sits on the shelves of finer wine merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a wine bottle; it is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, the same as nerve.

clue.text: Captain altered course in fit of severe anxiety

indicators.note: an altered word has been changed, its letters reordered

parts.note: a tack is a sailing course set relative to the wind

explanation.surface: A ship's captain changes direction suddenly in a fit of nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A panic attack is a sudden episode of intense fear with physical symptoms.

clue.text: Inventor discussed French symbol

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the Gallic rooster is a national symbol of France

explanation.surface: An inventor talked about the emblem of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Cockerell was the English engineer who invented the hovercraft.

clue.text: Hype in a rogue when seizing power produces moment of revelation

indicators.note: one set of letters seizes another, holding it inside
rogue means behaving erratically, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Hype in a dishonest figure grabbing power leads to a sudden insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like a noun for a scoundrel but signals the anagram, making EIHPANY; 'when seizing' puts the power letter inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden, striking realisation or insight.

clue.text: Only just how one measures rainfall?

definitions.meaning: rainfall is recorded by the inch in the imperial system

explanation.definitionFit: By inches is an idiom for narrowly, by a very small margin.

clue.text: Fine writing graphically represented

indicators.note: letters represented are presented again in a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Elegant handwriting shown in graphic form.
explanation.definitionFit: Calligraphy is the art of beautiful, decorative handwriting.

clue.text: Reportedly, pull top thing for protecting a boot

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to tow is to pull and a cap is a top, so the phrase is heard as tow cap

explanation.surface: Apparently, a pull-off top protects a boot.
explanation.definitionFit: A toecap is a reinforced cover on the front of a boot or shoe protecting the toes.

clue.text: Man in Rome regularly toured showing patience, perhaps

parts.note: vir is the Latin word for man

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one

explanation.surface: A Roman man touring often shows endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters of 'toured' gives TUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one example of a virtue, a moral good quality.

clue.text: Where one might see polar bears waiting in readiness?

definitions.text: Where one might see polar bears
definitions.meaning: polar bears live and hunt on sea ice

explanation.surface: Polar bears waiting, poised for their next meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put plans on ice is an idiom for holding them in reserve, ready for later use.

clue.text: Father messed up a pinny when grabbing good item in the kitchen

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: one set of letters grabs another, holding it inside
messed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad spoils an apron while snatching something good in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Messed up' rearranges A PINNY to YINPAN; 'when grabbing' puts G inside it. A pinny is a British word for an apron.
explanation.definitionFit: A frying pan is a common piece of kitchen equipment.

clue.text: Film critic on TV once snubbed opera

indicators.note: snubbed suggests a snub nose, cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Barry Norman presented BBC film review programmes for decades

explanation.surface: A former TV film critic dismisses an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is an opera by Bellini.

clue.text: Caught a place for surgery in the US lacking a medical tube

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: a word lacking something has had it taken away

parts.words: a place for surgery in the US
parts.note: an operating room is a theatre, spelt THEATER in American English

explanation.surface: An American operating theatre short of a medical tube is caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' removes the second A from the American spelling THEATER, leaving THETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a flexible tube inserted into the body to drain or deliver fluids.

clue.text: Disruption where one might play volleyball? About right

indicators.note: one word goes about, around, the other, enclosing it

parts.note: beach volleyball is played on sand

explanation.surface: A game of volleyball interrupted; is that right?
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a break or rupture, as in a breach of the peace.

clue.text: Rule out contralto appearing in opening passage

indicators.note: one piece appears inside the other

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece of music
C is the abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A conductor rules out the contralto singing in the opening passage.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent it or make it impossible in advance.

clue.text: South American dictators, not a model of industry, are lecherous types

indicators.note: not removes the following piece from the word

parts.note: tyrants are despotic rulers
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: Lazy South American despots are depicted as lechers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' takes ANT from TYRANTS, leaving TYRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyrs are mythological woodland creatures known for lust; by extension, lecherous men.
